thread.title: Ethan Salas Makes Splash with Two-Run Home Run to Propel Padres Past Rockies
thread.title_full: Ethan Salas Makes Splash with Two-Run Home Run to Propel Padres Past Rockies

author: sdut
title: Ethan Salas Makes Splash with Two-Run Home Run to Propel Padres Past Rockies
text:
The 20‑year‑old catcher Ethan Salas hit a two‑run homer in the fifth inning against the Colorado Rockies, becoming the youngest Padres player ever to homer twice in a game. The Padres secured a 9‑3 victory at Coors Field, with manager Craig Stammen praising Salas' performance and highlighting his contribution to the team's playoff push as the club sits near the bottom of the National League wild‑card race.
Ethan Salas gestures to the bullpen as he circles the bases after hitting a two-run home run in the fifth inning Wednesday against the Rockies.
The 20-year-old catcher is in the major leagues for the experience. And the Padres’ catcher of the future is being asked to produce now.
“We believe in Ethan, and we think he could really help us get to the playoffs and then in the playoffs,” manager Craig Stammen said Wednesday afternoon. “So we’ve got to make sure we’ve given him enough opportunity to be comfortable in those situations. ” Salas went out and helped the Padres beat the Rockies 9-3 by making himself extremely comfortable at Coors Field.
Salas turned around Robbie Ray’s night and turned around two pitches for his first two major league home runs.
“It means everything to me,” Salas said afterward. “It’s a good day. Thankfully, we got the win and got two good swings off today. They just happened to land over the fence.
”Salas became the youngest catcher to hit two home runs in a game since at least 1900 and the youngest Padres player ever to homer twice in a game. They began the day in possession of the final National League playoff spot, 2½ games ahead of the Diamondbacks, who were playing the Marlins on Wednesday night. The Padres remained 1½ games behind the Cubs and a game in back of the Phillies, who both won Wednesday.
It was largely thanks to their top prospect, who began the season in Double-A, was promoted to Triple-A on Aug. 1 and made his big-league debut on Sept. 2.
“He’s shown throughout his career that he has the ability to do that,” Stammen said. “And for the first time in the big leagues, he was able to show everybody what he’s made of.
” Salas, who was making his fourth start behind the plate and just got his first big-league hit with a triple on Sunday in San Francisco, led off Wednesday’s second inning by sending a fastball from Mason Adams a projected 426 feet to center field to extend the Padres’ lead to 3-1. His two-run homer off Nick Frasso, which just cleared the tall wall in right field, put the Padres up 8-1 in the fifth inning.
After Adams hit a batter, walked two and allowed two runs in a 32-pitch first inning, Ray’s first inning made the Rockies rookie look sharp. Ray also walked two batters and hit one, as the Rockies scored without getting a base hit and were about to load the bases with two outs.
But after a full-count sinker to Troy Johnston was initially judged by home plate umpire Cory Blaser to be the 16th ball in the 25 pitches Ray had thrown, Salas challenged the call. When the scoreboard graphic showed Ray’s pitch had nicked the outside corner to complete an inning-ending strikeout, Ray pointed emphatically at Salas, who pounded his glove. Salas then pounded the next pitch over the wall in center field.
And Ray, who said he slipped delivering a pitch early in the first and “it got in my head a little bit,” started throwing strikes. He got through the second inning allowing just a two-out single and went on to retire 10 straight batters before surrendering a single and Kyle Karros’ homer in the sixth.
After Ray completed his third quality start in eight outings for the Padres, David Morgan took over with a 9-3 lead, allowed a leadoff single in the seventh and then set down six straight. Yuki Matsui got the final three outs.
In addition to Salas’ three RBIs, the rest of the Padres big lead was built by Ty France’s sacrifice fly and Jake Cronenworth’s RBI single in the first inning, Dustin Harris’ run-scoring triple in the fourth, Samad Taylor’s two-run single in the fifth and an RBI double by France in the sixth. It was a reversal of a 9-3 loss on Tuesday in which the Padres had 11 hits but none of them in succession.
“I don’t think we took yesterday to heart,” said Jackson Merrill, who hit singles in his first three at-bats. “There’s gonna be games where it’s kind of hard to win the game. That was just one of those days yesterday. It was good to come back out today, score the first inning.
We scored the second one, too. It was just rapid-fire. That’s our team. Don’t back down.
”“Kind of feels like I’m playing now,” he said, “instead of just like being a part of the team just watching. It always feels good to put your two cents into the win. And just after the triple, everything kind of loosened up a little bit. And thankfully, today was a good day. ”
